expected.title: Smooth base change for prime-to-characteristic torsion etale cohomology
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proof must efface pulled-back injective sheaf cohomology, despite pullback not preserving injectivity. It reduces to relative curves, approximates by finite-type bases, passes through finite normalizations and controlled Galois covers of the generic fibre, then combines degree induction and dimension induction to kill the remaining support.

expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs the glued module as the kernel of a surjective difference map. It separates power torsion from the torsion-free quotient, controls Tor under base change and uses a comparison diagram to recover both local pieces, proving full faithfulness and essential surjectivity.

expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: After a nontrivial reduction to the projective line, one must compute cohomology over a strictly henselian local base using restricted injective resolutions. The proof compares the resulting stalks with closed-fibre cohomology and checks arbitrary field extensions, then promotes prime coefficients to all torsion via the injective criterion.

expected.title: Affineness of the maximal etale locus over excellent regular schemes
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proof must show the etale locus is affine even when its complement is not a divisor. It localizes over the regular target, uses purity and Hartshorne-Lichtenbaum vanishing to bound the structure-sheaf cohomological dimension of the locus, then applies the prior local affineness criterion to finish the dimension induction.

expected.title: Periodic Euler lengths equal orders of generic periodic determinants on one-dimensional support
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proof must reconcile finite-length cohomology with determinant scalars at all minimal support primes. After separating generic supports, carefully chosen good sequences in kernels and images must be lifted and adjusted to satisfy annihilator conditions, then compared through a common lattice so all length discrepancies exactly match the determinant order.

expected.title: Over an essentially finite-type local algebra of an arbitrary local ring, every base-linear map from a finite module to a flat module that is injective on the closed fibre is universally injective and forces flatness and finite presentation
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The module map is only A-linear, the base is arbitrary and the source is initially only finite over the essentially finite-type local algebra. The proof requires finitely generated flattening ideals, generic flatness stratification, a pure-spreadout/content construction, and a maximal-bad-prime argument before a nilpotent filtration establishes universal injectivity and finite presentation. These non-Noetherian finiteness and arbitrary base-linear mapping mechanisms go well beyond local flatness criteria from qualification algebra.

expected.title: Faltings annihilator theorem for local cohomology
expected.author: The Stacks Project Authors
expected.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a global annihilator by a double induction on cohomological degree and dimension-function strata. Spectral-sequence filtrations control successive powers of annihilators, and finite dualizing Ext supports produce uniform choices. The converse locates a minimal failing depth-codimension pair and proves its local cohomology cannot be annihilated.
